source.snippet: I've seen numbers like 75% of code at Google is AI generated, huge %s of code overall is AI generated, open source projects overwhelmed with 'slop' PR requests. It's pretty undeniable that AI code is here to stay — so on your teams / companies how are you managing staying up on PR reviews, and documentation?

problem_statement: Engineering teams using AI coding tools (Copilot, Cursor, etc.) have no reliable way to keep documentation and architectural context in sync as AI-generated code rapidly changes codebases, leading to stale docs and costly review bottlenecks.
target_segment: Engineering managers and senior developers at software companies (10–500 engineers) where AI-assisted coding is standard practice.
notes: Multiple community members engaging (4 points, 4 comments on a niche Ask HN). Poster frames it as a team/company problem, not personal curiosity. Companies already paying for AI coding tools and documentation platforms — the gap is glue between them. Opportunity: a bot or CI step that detects AI-generated code changes and auto-drafts or flags stale documentation, integrated into GitHub/GitLab PR workflow. Willingness-to-pay implied by existing spend on Copilot/Cursor + Confluence/Notion.
